To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the combination of high-quality observations with a well-chosen stochastic model and an efficient adjustment strategy allows for the determination of the position of the Onsalla 20 m radio-telescope reference point with a precision at the sub-milli-meter level.

the presented monitoring concept is capable of achieving the accuracy required by the global geodesic observing system and the presented concept can be used as a basis for a terrestrial monitoring concept for radio telescopes.

we were able to derive a coordinate-based network solution with an uncertainty budget that includes over 25 parameters and that we were able achieve sub-millimeter accuracy for the reference point of our radio telescope.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and implementation of a comprehensive stochastic model for a coordinate-based adjustment process.
a new concept for the adjustment of a terrestrial reference point, which is monitored with a very high frequency.
the monitoring of the radio telescope reference points in a true Cartesian reference system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the presented terrestrial monitoring concept is a powerful method to monitor radio telescope reference points with high precision and accuracy.
the presented monitoring concept is a very promising tool for the monitoring of radio telescope reference points.
a terrestrial monitoring campaign using a network of GNSS and reflectors can provide a reference point of a radio telescope with sub-millimeter accuracy, if the stochastic modeling is done properly.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the presented concept for terrestrial monitoring of a radio reference point using a local site network and reflectors mounted on the telescope can be used for high-accuracy monitoring of the telescope position.
we have shown that the presented concept for a terrestrial monitoring campaign is feasible and that the presented concept can serve as a basis for future monitoring campaigns.
we were able to demonstrate that the proposed monitoring concept can be applied to any radio telescope.
The main takeaway from our work is that

a network adjustment in a Cartesian global reference frame, including a comprehensive stochastic model, is a viable alternative to the conventional network adjustment in a spherical reference frame, which is based on the assumption that the Earth is a perfect sphere.

the presented approach for terrestrial reference point monitoring is capable of providing a reference point with a sub-millimeter accuracy, which is sufficient for the needs of modern radio astronomy.
a high-frequency terrestrial monitoring campaign can be performed with a very low number of observations and a very high accuracy.
